question: Estimate the number of unique mobile phone users in India.
idealClarificationQuestions: Unique people (not SIM cards) using a mobile phone? Yes — unique users.

expectedLogicalStructure.label: Frame the approach
expectedLogicalStructure.description: Total population minus those who don't use any phone (children, elderly, very poor).

expectedLogicalStructure.label: Calculate
expectedLogicalStructure.description: Adults who don't use any phone (elderly without family-shared use, very poor without access): ~5% of adults = ~60M.

expectedLogicalStructure.label: Calculate
expectedLogicalStructure.description: Unique mobile users: 1,450M - 200M - 60M = ~1,190M, but adjusting for shared use the unique person-with-access ~1.1B.

benchmarkAssumptions.parameter: Children under 8 (no phone of their own)
Adults who share phones (1 phone for 2 people in poor households)

benchmarkAssumptions.value: 1,450M - 200M - 60M = ~1,190M, but adjusting for shared use the unique person-with-access ~1.1B.

calculationFlow: Children under 8 (no phone of their own): ~14% = ~200M.
Adults who don't use any phone (elderly without family-shared use, very poor without access): ~5% of adults = ~60M.
Unique mobile users: 1,450M - 200M - 60M = ~1,190M, but adjusting for shared use the unique person-with-access ~1.1B.
